scenarios.title: Rookie Dinner
scenarios.text: The veterans 'invite' the rookies to cover the team dinner at a fancy steakhouse.

choices.label: Pay for the whole thing
choices.result: Expensive, but the vets love you.

choices.label: Split it with the other rookies
choices.result: Fair and friendly.

choices.label: Politely pass
choices.result: A couple of veterans give you the cold shoulder.

scenarios.title: Agent Meeting
scenarios.text: Three agencies want to represent you. Each one has a pitch.

choices.label: Sign with the big agency
choices.result: Big name, big plans.

choices.label: Hire a small, careful agent
choices.result: Fewer promises, more attention.

choices.label: Represent yourself
choices.result: Saves money. Costs sleep.

scenarios.title: Contract Talks
scenarios.text: Your agent says the team wants to talk about an extension.

choices.label: Push for top dollar
choices.result: Talks get tense.

choices.label: Take a team-friendly deal
choices.result: Teammates notice. Management does too.

choices.label: Wait until the season ends
choices.result: Bet on yourself.

choices.label: Let the fans make your case
choices.result: Your public profile does the negotiating.

scenarios.title: Postgame Questions
scenarios.text: After a missed kick last week, reporters are waiting at your locker.

choices.label: Own the miss
choices.result: Straight answers earn respect.

choices.label: Blame the conditions
choices.result: The quote doesn't land well.

choices.label: Decline to talk
choices.result: You skip the circus.

choices.label: Turn it into a rallying cry
choices.result: The locker room plays your quote all week.

scenarios.title: Family and Finances
scenarios.text: Relatives keep asking for loans now that you're a pro.

choices.label: Set a budget with an advisor
choices.result: Clear rules, fewer awkward calls.

choices.label: Help everyone out
choices.result: Generous, and stressful.

choices.label: Say no to everyone
choices.result: Peace for your wallet, tension at home.

scenarios.title: Team Hospital Visit
scenarios.text: The team is visiting the children's hospital this week.

choices.label: Stay all afternoon
choices.result: You'll remember this one forever.

choices.label: Join for the group photo
choices.result: A quick, kind visit.

choices.label: Skip it for treatment
choices.result: You get extra recovery time.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry
scenarios.text: Your holder wants extra time to work on timing this week.

choices.label: Extra reps every day
choices.result: Snap, hold, kick. Perfect timing.

choices.label: Take a recovery day instead
choices.result: Your leg feels brand new.

choices.label: Study the opponent's stadium
choices.result: You know every gust in that building.

scenarios.title: Cold Snap
scenarios.text: Forecast says single digits and wind for Sunday.

choices.label: Practice outside all week
choices.result: Your leg learns the cold.

choices.label: Practice indoors
choices.result: Warm and accurate. Not ready for the wind.

choices.label: Ask the equipment staff for help
choices.result: Heated capes and the right cleats.

scenarios.title: Trade Rumors
scenarios.text: Sports radio says the team might trade for another kicker.

choices.label: Tune out the noise
choices.result: Kick, sleep, repeat.

choices.label: Ask the coach directly
choices.result: He says you're his guy. For now.

choices.label: Read every rumor online
choices.result: It's all you think about.

scenarios.title: The Folder Follows You
scenarios.text: Your first month as a pro, the team's player-development director calls you in. Your college record followed you here, and the club wants to know what kind of player it signed.

authoring.premise: The team's player-development director calls the rookie in: the college record followed you here.
authoring.note: Reads the college wrong-path flags (planned_pro_reads in tools/college_graph/college_design.json).

choices.label: Ask for a weekly check-in
choices.result: You suggest a weekly check-in yourself and hand over your college coach's number. The director writes it in the file: rookie asked for structure.

choices.label: Say college is over
choices.result: You say the folder belongs to a different person and you'd rather be judged on what you do here. The director says that's fair. The file stays open.

choices.label: Bring your own copy
choices.result: You bring a copy of your college record with your own notes in the margins: what happened and what changed. The director keeps it and tells {coach} to stop worrying.
choices.lock_text: having already faced your record honestly

scenarios.title: The Old Crowd
scenarios.text: Three guys you used to run with in college show up in your new city on a Friday with a hotel suite booked and a plan for your first paycheck. Your phone has been buzzing since noon.

authoring.premise: Old college running buddies show up in your new city with a hotel suite and a plan for your first paycheck.
authoring.note: Reads the college wrong-path flags (planned_pro_reads in tools/college_graph/college_design.json).

choices.label: Dinner, then home
choices.result: You buy them dinner, laugh about the old days and are home by ten. They call you boring. You're at the facility at seven.

choices.label: Don't answer
choices.result: You let the phone buzz and stay in. It's lonely, and it's the first weekend in a while you don't regret anything.

choices.label: Go out with them
choices.result: You go out. Saturday's photos end up online, a team official calls on Monday, and {coach} hears about it before you're in the building.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Symposium
scenarios.text: The league's rookie symposium wants a player to speak about a mistake from college and what came after. The team's player-development director thinks your story is the one the rookies need to hear.

authoring.premise: The league's rookie symposium wants a player to talk about a college mistake and what came after.
authoring.note: Reads the college wrong-path flags (planned_pro_reads in tools/college_graph/college_design.json).

choices.label: Tell the whole story
choices.result: You stand in front of two hundred rookies and tell them about your worst college year without making yourself the hero. Afterward, a line of players waits to talk to you.

choices.label: Tell the safe version
choices.result: You give the version with the details smoothed over. It goes fine, and nobody waits afterward.

choices.label: Say no thanks
choices.result: You say you'd rather not relive it in front of a room. The director understands and asks someone else.

scenarios.title: The Reporter's Question
scenarios.text: At your first open locker room, a beat reporter skips the kicking questions and asks about your college record: 'Do you think the stories about you are fair?'

authoring.premise: At your first open locker room, a reporter skips the kicking questions and asks about your college record.
authoring.note: Reads the college wrong-path flags (planned_pro_reads in tools/college_graph/college_design.json).

choices.label: Answer it straight
choices.result: You say the stories are true, you're not proud of them and you'd rather be judged on what comes next. The quote runs in full, and it's the least dramatic thing in the paper.

choices.label: Say no comment
choices.result: You say you're only taking football questions. The reporter writes that you 'declined to address' your past, which reads worse than anything you could have said.

choices.label: Push back
choices.result: You say the stories were overblown and the reporter should do some homework. It's the most-shared clip of the week, and {coach} asks you to stop by the office.

scenarios.title: Rookie Camp
scenarios.text: Camp opens with four kickers on the roster and one job. The special teams coordinator has called you by the wrong name twice, and {coach} hasn't called you anything at all.

authoring.premise: Camp opens with four kickers on the roster and one job. The veteran special teams coordinator calls you by the wrong name twice.

choices.label: Be the first one on the field
choices.result: You're stretching on the field at six every morning before the trainers unlock the door. By the second week, {coach} knows your name and uses it.

choices.label: Learn the room before the field
choices.result: You spend the first week listening: who the veterans trust, which snapper the coaches like, where the rookies sit at lunch. It's slow, and nothing in that locker room surprises you after it.

choices.label: Kick like it's already yours
choices.result: You walk in like the job is yours and kick like it too. Two veterans love it. One of the other kickers stops talking to you entirely.

choices.label: Do what got you here
choices.result: You've been in rooms where nobody expected anything from you. You kick, you say little, and you keep a notebook of every correction. {coach} borrows the notebook in week two.
choices.lock_text: having trained with a pro or rebuilt a reputation before

scenarios.title: The Kicker You're Replacing
scenarios.text: The kicker whose job you're taking has been here eleven years. His locker is next to yours, and he can make your first month easy or impossible.

authoring.premise: The kicker whose job you're taking has been here eleven years. He can make your first month easy or impossible.

choices.label: Ask him to teach you
choices.result: You ask him straight out how he lasted eleven years. He stares at you for a while, then starts talking and doesn't stop for an hour.

choices.label: Compete and keep your distance
choices.result: You stay polite and give him nothing. Every kick in camp becomes a quiet contest, and both of you get better.

choices.label: Freeze him out
choices.result: You sit with the younger players, laugh at the right jokes about his age and let the room decide who's in charge. You win the room. You also notice who stopped laughing.

scenarios.title: Your First Real Payday
scenarios.text: Your first real paycheck lands, and it has more zeros than {parent} made in a year. Your phone starts buzzing before you've finished reading the number.

authoring.premise: Your first real paycheck lands, and it has more zeros than {parent} made in a year.

choices.label: Save most of it
choices.result: You put most of it into an account you promise not to touch and buy one thing: a mattress that isn't from a dorm. It's dull, and you sleep very well.

choices.label: Spend it like you earned it
choices.result: You buy the car, the watch and dinner for the whole rookie class. It feels incredible for about a month.

choices.label: Pay off {parent}'s debts
choices.result: You call {parent} and ask for the number on every bill. He refuses twice and gives in the third time. The calls home sound different after that.

choices.label: Split it the way you always have
choices.result: You do what you did with your first paycheck at sixteen, just with more zeros: a third saved, a third home, a third yours. It's an old habit, and it holds.
choices.lock_text: having handled your first paychecks wisely

scenarios.title: Rookie Duties
scenarios.text: The veterans hand the rookies a list: breakfast for the unit every Friday, carrying the pads, a song on the team plane. Most of it is fun. One item, a stunt in a hotel hallway, isn't.

authoring.premise: The veterans hand the rookies a list: breakfast for the unit every Friday, the luggage, the karaoke on the team plane. Some of it is fun. One item isn't.

choices.label: Do the list, skip the stunt
choices.result: You do every chore with a grin and tell the captain, privately, you're not doing the hallway stunt. He shrugs and crosses it off.

choices.label: Do all of it
choices.result: You do everything on the list, the stunt included. The veterans cheer, a rookie gets hurt doing the same one, and the coaches hold a meeting about it.

choices.label: Turn the song into a show
choices.result: You go all in on the plane song, with costumes. It's the best one in years, and the veterans stop giving you the worst chores.

choices.label: Fix the list with the captain
choices.result: You ran this kind of tradition in college, so you sit down with the captain and rewrite the stunt into something nobody gets hurt doing. It's a quiet win.
choices.lock_text: having run freshman traditions in college

scenarios.title: The Long Snapper
scenarios.text: The long snapper has been in the league fourteen years and has opinions about everything, including your warmup, your shoes and the way you say 'hold'.

authoring.premise: The long snapper has been in the league fourteen years and has opinions about everything, including your warmup.

choices.label: Listen to every opinion
choices.result: You let him talk. Half of it is nonsense. The other half fixes a timing problem you didn't know you had.

choices.label: Push back on the warmup
choices.result: You tell him your warmup isn't changing. He respects it more than you expected and starts timing his snaps to it.

choices.label: Keep it professional
choices.result: You say thanks, keep it short and do your own thing. The snaps are fine. The friendship never quite starts.

scenarios.title: Curfew on the Road
scenarios.text: First road trip. Curfew is eleven, and the veterans say curfew is for rookies who want to stay rookies. Three of them are already in the lobby.

authoring.premise: First road trip. Curfew is eleven, and the veterans say curfew is for rookies who want to stay rookies.
authoring.note: Pressure scene: clean no. The wrong choice sets pro strike stayed_out_pro.

choices.label: Stay in
choices.result: You order room service, watch film and are asleep by ten-thirty. At breakfast you're the only rookie who isn't wearing sunglasses.

choices.label: Go to dinner, back by eleven
choices.result: You go to dinner with the veterans, laugh at their stories and leave before dessert. A couple of them call you a rookie. A couple of them nod.

choices.label: Go out with them
choices.result: You go out and come back at three. Bed check was at eleven, and your name is on the list {coach} reads out at breakfast.

scenarios.title: Where You Live
scenarios.text: Half the roster lives in the same glass tower downtown, with a rooftop pool and a doorman who knows everyone's name. The rent is a quarter of your salary.

authoring.premise: Half the roster lives in the same glass tower downtown. The rent is a quarter of your salary.

choices.label: Rent something modest
choices.result: You rent a two-bedroom twenty minutes from the facility, above a bakery. The teammates call it 'the bakery'. You save more in a month than some of them save in a year, and the commute is short.

choices.label: Move into the tower
choices.result: You sign the lease in the tower. The pool parties are legendary, the elevator rides are full of teammates, and the rent comes out of every check like a tax.

choices.label: Room with a teammate
choices.result: You split a place with another rookie. It's cheaper, louder, and you never eat dinner alone.

scenarios.title: Homesick in {town}
scenarios.text: Nobody in {town} knows your name yet, and the apartment is very quiet on Tuesday nights.

authoring.premise: Nobody in {town} knows your name yet, and the apartment is very quiet on Tuesday nights.

choices.label: Call home every night
choices.result: You call home every night for a week. {parent} starts saving up stories for you, like he used to before school.

choices.label: Make the city yours
choices.result: You pick one new neighborhood every Tuesday and walk it until dinner. By October, {town} has a coffee shop that knows your order.

choices.label: Bury it in work
choices.result: You spend every quiet night in the film room. You're the best-prepared rookie on the roster and the loneliest.

choices.label: Keep the Sunday call
choices.result: You kept the Sunday call through four years of college, and you keep it now. The first Sunday in {town}, {sibling} answers and talks for an hour.
choices.lock_text: having promised to call home every week

scenarios.title: The Practice Squad Friend
scenarios.text: The receiver you've eaten lunch with since camp gets cut on a Tuesday morning. At noon he's still sitting in his car in the players' lot.

authoring.premise: The receiver you've been eating lunch with since camp gets cut on a Tuesday morning. He's still in the parking lot at noon.

choices.label: Sit in the car with him
choices.result: You knock on the window and sit in the passenger seat for an hour. You don't say much. He drives away a little steadier.

choices.label: Make a call for him
choices.result: You call a coach you know at another club and say the receiver's name twice. He gets a workout the next week.

choices.label: Leave him alone
choices.result: You walk past to your own car. It's not your business, and it could be you next year. You think about it the whole drive home.

scenarios.title: Meeting the Owner
scenarios.text: The owner throws a party for the rookies at his house and spends twenty minutes telling you exactly what kickers are worth, which is not much.

authoring.premise: The owner throws a party for the rookies at his house and spends twenty minutes telling you what kickers are worth.

choices.label: Smile and agree
choices.result: You smile, agree and get a second drink of lemonade. He likes you. You feel slightly worse about yourself on the drive home.

choices.label: Make him laugh
choices.result: You tell him kickers are the only players who show up to work every week without hurting anyone. He laughs harder than you expected and remembers your name.

choices.label: Tell him he's wrong
choices.result: You tell him, politely, that he's wrong, and why. The room goes quiet. {coach} hears about it by Monday.

scenarios.title: The Quote
scenarios.text: You said something careless to a beat reporter about the kicker you replaced, and it's the headline on the team's biggest fan site.

authoring.premise: You said something careless to a beat reporter about the veteran you replaced, and it's the headline.

choices.label: Apologize to his face
choices.result: You find him and apologize in person, no excuses. He accepts it more gracefully than you would have.

choices.label: Say it was taken out of context
choices.result: You tell another reporter it was out of context. The original reporter posts the full recording.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.result: You let it blow over. It does, in about a week, and the veterans remember it a while longer.

choices.label: Handle it the way you learned to
choices.result: You've done this before. You call the reporter back, own the quote, and apologize to the veteran before lunch. It's over by dinner.
choices.lock_text: having been through a public mistake before

scenarios.title: Your First Autograph Line
scenarios.text: A kid in a jersey with your number on it is first in line at the autograph table. You didn't know they made your number.

authoring.premise: A kid in a jersey with your number on it is first in line. You didn't know they made your number.

choices.label: Take your time with him
choices.result: You sign the jersey, the ball and his little brother's hat, and ask him about his own team. The line behind him gets longer and nobody minds.

choices.label: Ask his parents for a photo
choices.result: You ask for a photo and post it with his first name and no last name. It's the best-liked thing you've ever posted.

choices.label: Keep the line moving
choices.result: You sign, smile and keep the line moving like the team's staff asked. Two hundred people get an autograph, and none of them get a moment.

scenarios.title: Rookie Year Ends
scenarios.text: The season's over. The locker room empties in an afternoon, and you realize you have no idea what pros do in the offseason.

authoring.premise: The season's over. The locker room empties in an afternoon, and you realize you have no idea what pros do in the offseason.

choices.label: Ask the veterans
choices.result: You ask three veterans how they spend the offseason and steal the best of each plan. It's the best summer of training you've had.

choices.label: Go home for a month
choices.result: You go home and do nothing for a month: {parent}'s cooking, old friends, your old bedroom. You come back rested and a little out of shape.

choices.label: Train like you're still in camp
choices.result: You never stop. Six days a week, all summer. By August your leg is the strongest it's been, and you're tired before camp starts.

scenarios.title: The Second-Year Wall
scenarios.text: Year two. The novelty is gone, the scouting reports on you are thicker, and your legs remember every kick of last season.

authoring.premise: Year two. The novelty is gone, the scouting reports on you are thicker, and your legs feel every one of last season's kicks.

choices.label: Change something small
choices.result: You change one thing, a half-step in your approach, and chart it for a month. It takes, and it surprises the coaches watching you.

choices.label: Change nothing
choices.result: You decide last year's routine earned you this year, and you keep every piece of it. Some weeks it works perfectly. Some weeks it's just a routine.

choices.label: Take on a rookie
choices.result: You take the new rookie specialist under your wing, like someone did for you. It costs you time, and it makes the room yours.

scenarios.title: Your Story, Secondhand
scenarios.text: A college teammate calls from his rookie symposium: they told a story about a player who owned his mistakes and came back, and it sounded a lot like you.

authoring.premise: A former teammate from college calls from his rookie symposium: they told a story about someone who sounds a lot like you.
authoring.note: College callback scene: opens only for players with a college comeback; pairs with pro_rookie_symposium.

choices.label: Tell him the real version
choices.result: You tell him the parts that didn't make the speech: the bad nights, the early workouts, the people who wouldn't look at you for a while. He goes quiet and then thanks you.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and say they must have meant someone else. It's easier than talking about it, and you feel it all week.

choices.label: Call the people who helped
choices.result: You hang up and call the coach who gave you the chance. The coach doesn't say much, and doesn't need to.

authoring.premise: Three weeks of misses in practice and the coaches have stopped talking to you about it, which is worse.
authoring.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15 weeks). Locks open with experience (kick_slumps, age).

authoring.premise: {coach} watches your warmup with folded arms and doesn't say a word.
You're inactive this week. Your name is on the board, and your helmet is in your locker.
authoring.note: Every engine flag is sticky from high school, so the present-state check is needed.

authoring.premise: You're active again. The kicker who replaced you is clearing out his stall.
You haven't missed in a month, and everyone wants to talk about it except you.
The specialists have a superstition: nobody says the streak out loud. A rookie just said it.
Your name is on the national list for the league's best kicker, and the team's PR staff has eleven requests for you.
The league invites you to the long-distance contest at the all-star week.
authoring.note: kick_challenge (competition) per the gameplay handoff.

authoring.premise: The afternoon talk show has a segment called 'Cut the Kicker', and your {parent} listens to it every day.
Your foot won't swing through the ball in practice. Not tired, not hurt, just stuck.
A private coach who rebuilt three pro kickers offers you his offseason, for a price.
{coach} plays every miss of your season back to back in an empty meeting room.
Your plant leg is sore in a way the trainers can't find on a scan.

scenarios.title: The Backup Wants Your Job
scenarios.text: {backup} is on the practice squad and has been kicking very well where the coaches can see.

authoring.premise: {backup} is on the practice squad and has been kicking very well where the coaches can see.

choices.label: Kick with {backup}
choices.result: You ask {backup} to share your warmups. It makes you both better, and it makes the coaches' decision harder, which is fine.

choices.label: Out-work {backup}
choices.result: You stay later than {backup} every day for a month. The coaches notice the hours more than the kicks.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You decide the practice squad isn't your problem. Your kicking stays the same, and so does the whispering.

scenarios.title: The New Holder Midseason
scenarios.text: {holder} is hurt, and the replacement holder is a backup quarterback who has never held for a kick.

authoring.premise: {holder} is hurt, and the replacement holder is a backup quarterback who has never held for a kick.

choices.label: Teach the new holder
choices.result: You stay after practice every day with the backup quarterback until the laces spin right. By Friday the holds are clean.

choices.label: Ask for a different holder
choices.result: You ask {coach} for the punter instead. The coach agrees, and the quarterback looks relieved.

choices.label: Visit {holder}
choices.result: You visit {holder} in the training room and bring the new holder along for a lesson. Two holders and a kicker in one cramped room, laughing.

authoring.premise: Your contract pays a bonus if you hit 90 percent this season, and your agent keeps texting you the math.
The club signs a kicker with a bigger leg and a lower salary, and puts him at the locker next to yours.
authoring.note: Prime-age version; PRO_133 is the veteran version.

authoring.premise: Every kick in practice now feels like a negotiation.

scenarios.title: The Kick Everyone Saw
scenarios.text: A clip of you in a practice-field trick shot, the ball off the crossbar and into a trash can, goes around the league.

authoring.premise: A clip of you in a practice-field trick shot goes around the league.
authoring.note: Practice clip only; no game result.

choices.label: Make a few more
choices.result: You film a series with the specialists. It's fun, the club's social media team loves it, and the coaches don't.

choices.label: Let it be one clip
choices.result: You thank people and leave it there. It fades in a week.

choices.label: Use it for charity
choices.result: You turn the clip into a charity challenge: a donation for every kid who sends in their own trick shot.

authoring.premise: You snapped at {holder}, ignored {coach} and skipped the team meal. It's been that kind of week.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: Prove It
scenarios.text: It's the last year of your rookie deal, and the front office wants to see one more season before it talks.

authoring.premise: It's the last year of your rookie deal, and the front office wants to see one more season before they talk.

choices.label: Put your head down
choices.result: You stop reading anything about contracts and kick. Your agent handles the rest, and the season feels lighter for it.

choices.label: Ask {coach} what they want
choices.result: You ask {coach} exactly what the club needs from you this year. The answer is two things, and both are fixable.

choices.label: Push for a deal now
choices.result: You have your agent push for an extension before the season. The club says no, politely, and remembers that you asked.

authoring.premise: This is the contract that sets up your family for life, if you earn it this season.
At your age, the next contract is one year at a time, and everyone in the building knows it.
The club wants you back. Your agent wants to wait for the market.
The club offers less than the market, and asks you to take it because you're family here.

scenarios.title: The Holdout Talk
scenarios.text: Your agent slides the club's offer across a restaurant table: less than a kicker in your division got last spring, with a pay cut in year two. 'We hold out,' your agent says. 'You stay home from camp until they pay you what you're worth.'

authoring.premise: Your agent says the only way to get paid is to stay home from camp.
authoring.note: A temptation, not a mechanic: the game has no holdouts. Holding firm costs retention and the coach.

choices.label: Sign it and say why
choices.result: You sign, then tell your agent you'd rather kick for a fair number than sit at home waiting for a better one. Your agent calls it leaving money on the table. {coach} calls it the best news of the week.

choices.label: Hold out
choices.result: You stay home when camp opens. The club fines you every day, talk radio calls you greedy, and two weeks later you sign for a little more and walk into a locker room that moved on without you.

choices.label: Call the general manager yourself
choices.result: You call the general manager directly, which agents hate. You get a better guarantee in year two and an agent who sulks for a month.

choices.label: Ask for the honest read
choices.result: The agent you hired for honesty admits the offer is fair for a kicker and a holdout would cost more than it gains. You sign, and you don't regret it.
choices.lock_text: having hired an agent who tells you the truth

scenarios.title: Starting Over
scenarios.text: The last club let you go at the end of camp: a ten-minute meeting, a plastic bag for your cleats and a security guard who walked you to the parking lot. Ten days later you're in a stranger's locker room, and the kicker you're replacing still has his name above the stall.

authoring.premise: The last club let you go. A week ago you were cleaning out a locker; today you're in a stranger's locker room in a city you've never visited.
authoring.note: Opens after any release or cut (the engine's failed_tryouts list), in the first weeks at the next club. Tone-check scene (being cut at the end of camp).

choices.label: Learn every name by Friday
choices.result: You learn every name in the specialists' room by Friday and buy the long snapper lunch. Nobody here owes you anything, and by Sunday a few of them act like they might.

choices.label: Say nothing and kick

scenarios.title: Summer at Home
scenarios.text: Your first offseason back home, and everyone at the grocery store wants to talk about one kick.

authoring.premise: Your first offseason back home, and everyone at the grocery store wants to talk about one kick.

choices.label: Enjoy being home
choices.result: You sleep in your old bedroom, eat {parent}'s cooking and let the town make a fuss. It's the best month you've had in a year.

choices.label: Train at your old high school
choices.result: You train on your old high school field every morning. The kids on the team start showing up to watch.

choices.label: Hide from the attention
choices.result: You stay in, see a few friends, and avoid the grocery store. It's quiet, and a little lonely.

authoring.premise: A youth camp asks you to coach for a week. The kids kick terribly and have more fun than you've had in years.
A real vacation, no phones, and a family that's not used to having you around for a whole week.
Four friends are getting married this summer, and every one of them wants you to give a toast.
The doctors say a small surgery now saves your next three seasons. The recovery takes the whole summer.
A young kicker from a rival club asks to train with you this summer.
You sign up for a class at the community college, something that has nothing to do with football.
Your college invites you back for spring practice. The kicking net is in the same place.
You're buying a house, and every room is an argument about how long you'll stay in this city.
For one offseason, you put the bag in the closet and don't touch a ball for six weeks.
A fan convention wants you for a signing weekend. The line includes people who've followed you since high school.
Friends plan a climbing trip. Your contract has a clause about 'dangerous activities'.
A new trainer wants to rebuild how you move, from the ground up, at an age when most kickers stop changing.
It might be your last offseason as a player. Every summer routine feels a little heavier.
Your hometown throws you a parade after your best season. {parent} rides in the front car.
Your old private kicking coach calls with an idea about your plant foot.
The club's charity golf event, with donors, owners and one teammate who's had too much sun.
A company offers you an off-season job in sales. It's real work, and it would be good to know you can do it.
The family reunion. Everyone wants a photo, and one uncle wants a loan.
You come back from the off-season heavier than the club likes, and the strength coach has a scale ready.
You're the oldest player in the locker room, and the young ones bring their problems to you.
A rookie calls you 'unc' at practice. It sticks.
Your first pro holder is a coach now, and is coaching against you on Sunday.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Grew Up Watching

authoring.premise: The kicker whose poster hung in your bedroom is at your game, and asks to meet you.
The league moves the extra-point line again, and the young kickers are thrilled.
The club's old stadium is being torn down after this season. You've played more games there than anyone left on the roster.
Your two-hundredth game as a pro. The club makes a video, and you can't watch it.
Your rookie class has a reunion. Half of them have bad knees and good stories.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Wears Your Number

authoring.premise: A rookie at another club wears your number and says you're the reason.

scenarios.title: A Teammate's Kid Asks for Advice

authoring.premise: A teammate's teenage kid kicks for a high school team and wants your advice.
The head coach who drafted you is fired. You're still here.
The club's analysts present a chart: your leg is getting older faster than you are.
Your longest kick in practice is five yards shorter than last year. The coaches haven't said it, but they've noticed.
The owner who signed you dies, and the family asks you to speak.

scenarios.title: A Midnight Call From an Old Teammate

authoring.premise: A teammate from your rookie year is broke and calls you at midnight.
Retired players are organizing for better health care, and they want a current player at the meeting.
A lineman you played with for years doesn't remember your name at a reunion.

scenarios.title: The Last of Your Draft Class

authoring.premise: You're the last player from your draft class still in the league.

scenarios.title: The Kid Who Was Born on Draft Day

authoring.premise: A rookie mentions he was born the week you were drafted.
Turning forty in the league: a birthday cake in the locker room and a question in every interview.

authoring.premise: The team votes for captains, and for the first time a kicker is on the ballot.
Your agent says this is the contract that matters, and the club agrees, eventually.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Coach

authoring.premise: Your holder retires and joins the coaching staff. Now they're your boss.
Your biggest sponsor wants to renew, with new conditions.
You organize a charity game in your hometown with players from five clubs.
A rival club's general manager makes it clear they'd pay more, next time you're free.
Nothing's wrong. That's the problem: practice feels like a job, and the job feels like nothing.

scenarios.title: The Kid Who Copies Your Routine

authoring.premise: A high school kicker's video goes around: he copies your routine down to the last step.
Your closest teammate is holding out for a new contract, and wants you to say something publicly.
The new special teams coordinator's son is a kicker on the practice squad.
Ten years in the league. The pension kicks in, and so does the question of how many more.
Your first prime-time game in years, and the broadcast crew wants an interview at the hotel.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Advice
scenarios.text: An eleven-year veteran pulls you aside after practice with a few rules for surviving the league.

authoring.premise: An established teammate pulls you aside with a few rules for surviving the league.

choices.label: Write them down
choices.result: You write every rule down that night. Some are about kicking. Most are about money and people.

choices.label: Ask about the hard years
choices.result: You ask about his worst season. He talks for an hour, and you learn more than the rules.

choices.label: Nod and forget them
choices.result: You nod politely and forget them by dinner. Three of them come back to you later, the hard way.

scenarios.title: The First Media Interview
scenarios.text: Local reporters catch you at your locker before you've learned what not to say.

authoring.premise: Local reporters catch you at your locker before you've learned what not to say.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: You give short, polite answers and nothing quotable. The story is boring, which {coach} likes.

choices.label: Be yourself
choices.result: You joke, tell a story about your college holder and admit you're nervous. The reporters like you, and so do the fans.

choices.label: Say something bold
choices.result: You say you'll be the best kicker in the league in three years. It's the headline, and the veterans tape it to your locker.

scenarios.title: The Missed Opportunity
scenarios.text: A bad practice in front of the whole staff, and by lunch someone in the building is asking about your roster spot.

authoring.premise: A bad practice in front of the whole staff, and someone in the building is already asking about your roster spot.

choices.label: Ask {coach} what happened
choices.result: You go to {coach} after lunch and ask what the staff saw. It's a timing issue, and it's fixable.

choices.label: Stay late and fix it
choices.result: You stay until the field lights come on, kicking until it feels right again.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.result: You tell yourself one practice doesn't matter and go home. Tomorrow is better, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Agent Calls
scenarios.text: Your agent calls to talk about your contract, your future and a few things you'd rather not hear: what rookies get cut for.

authoring.premise: Your agent calls to talk about your contract, your future and a few things you'd rather not hear.

choices.label: Listen to all of it
choices.result: You listen to the whole list without interrupting. It's sobering, and you know exactly what to avoid.

choices.label: Ask for a plan
choices.result: You ask your agent for a real plan for the next two years. You get one, in writing.

choices.label: Cut the call short
choices.result: You say you're focused on kicking and cut the call short. Your agent sends the list by email anyway.

scenarios.title: The First Endorsement
scenarios.text: A local car wash offers you your first sponsorship: a billboard, a few appearances and a small check.

authoring.premise: A local business offers you your first sponsorship: a billboard, a few appearances, a small check.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result: You sign. The billboard goes up by the highway, and every teammate sends you a photo of it.

choices.label: Ask your agent first
choices.result: You send it to your agent, who negotiates the appearances down and the check up.

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.result: You turn it down to keep your weeks clear. Your weeks stay clear, and your account stays the same.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Request
scenarios.text: An old friend from home asks you for money, and you can tell it took a lot to ask.

authoring.premise: Someone from home asks you for money, and you can tell it took a lot to ask.

choices.label: Give it, no questions
choices.result: You send it the same day and don't ask what it's for. Your friend cries on the phone.

choices.label: Ask what it's for
choices.result: You ask what it's for. It's rent, and you pay the landlord directly, which makes both of you feel better.

choices.label: Say no kindly
choices.result: You say you can't, kindly. It's true and it isn't, and the next phone call is shorter.

scenarios.title: The Long-Distance Relationship
scenarios.text: {love_interest} is three states away, and your schedule doesn't have room for flights.

authoring.premise: {love_interest} is three states away, and your schedule doesn't have room for flights.

choices.label: Fly them in on the bye
choices.result: You fly {love_interest} in for the bye week. It's short and it's enough until the next one.

choices.label: Video calls every night
choices.result: You set a video call every night at ten, no matter what. Some nights it's five minutes, and it holds.

choices.label: Let the season come first
choices.result: You tell {love_interest} the season comes first, and you'll make it up in the offseason. They say okay, too quickly.

scenarios.title: The Coach's Criticism
scenarios.text: {coach} tells you, in front of the specialists, that your preparation isn't professional yet.

authoring.premise: {coach} tells you, in front of the specialists, that your preparation isn't professional yet.

choices.label: Ask for specifics
choices.result: You ask {coach} for the three things that would make it professional. You get them, and you do them.

choices.label: Prove it with work
choices.result: You say nothing and show up an hour earlier every day for a month.

choices.label: Push back
choices.result: You tell {coach} your preparation got you here. The specialists go very quiet.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Mistake
scenarios.text: You trip over a cable at the team's charity event and take down a whole table of desserts, on camera.

authoring.premise: You make an embarrassing mistake at a team event, and the veterans won't let you forget it.

choices.label: Laugh at yourself
choices.result: You laugh first, help clean up and post the clip yourself. It's the most popular thing you've ever posted.

choices.label: Apologize to the organizers
choices.result: You apologize to the organizers and offer to pay for the desserts. They're touched, and invite you back next year.

choices.label: Hope nobody saw
choices.result: You slip out early and hope nobody saw. The veterans saw, and they won't let it go all season. You spend the rest of the night at the kicking net instead.

scenarios.title: The First Charity Event
scenarios.text: The club sends you to represent it at a community center's reading day, and nobody tells you what to say.

authoring.premise: The club sends you to represent it at a community event, and nobody tells you what to say.

choices.label: Read to the kids
choices.result: You sit on the floor and read three books in funny voices. The kids want a fourth.

choices.label: Talk about school
choices.result: You talk about how hard school was for you and why you kept going. A teacher thanks you afterward.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: You smile, sign autographs and leave on time. It's fine. Nobody remembers it.

scenarios.title: The Social Media Post
scenarios.text: An old post from college resurfaces the week your name starts showing up in the papers. It's not terrible, but it's not who you want to be.

authoring.premise: An old post resurfaces the week your name starts showing up in the papers.

choices.label: Delete it and apologize
choices.result: You delete it and post a short apology in your own words. It fades in a day.

choices.label: Leave it up
choices.result: You leave it up and say nothing. It keeps resurfacing for a month.

choices.label: Ask the club's media staff
choices.result: You ask the club's media staff what to do. They walk you through it, and nobody remembers it by Friday.

choices.label: Do what worked before
choices.result: You've been through this before, so you delete it, apologize in two sentences and go to practice. It's over by lunch.
choices.lock_text: having handled an old post the right way before

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Party
scenarios.text: A teammate's party the night before an early workday, and the whole rookie class is going.

authoring.premise: A teammate's party the night before an early workday, and the whole rookie class is going.

choices.label: Go for an hour
choices.result: You show up, say hello to everyone and leave before ten. Two rookies call you boring. You're the only one awake in the morning meeting.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.result: You stay home and get nine hours of sleep. You hear the stories at breakfast and feel fine about missing them.

choices.label: Stay until the end
choices.result: You stay until three. The workday is a blur, and {coach} asks if you're sick.

scenarios.title: The New City
scenarios.text: You can explore {town} or stay in your apartment with the blinds closed.

authoring.premise: You can explore {town} or stay in your apartment with the blinds closed.

choices.label: Explore one neighborhood a week
choices.result: You pick a neighborhood every week and walk it. By midseason you know {town} better than some teammates who grew up here.

choices.label: Find one place to belong
choices.result: You find one diner, one gym and one coffee shop and become a regular at all three.

choices.label: Stay in
choices.result: You stay in your apartment between practices. It's restful, and {town} stays a stranger.

scenarios.title: The Family Visit
scenarios.text: {parent} and {sibling} want to visit for a weekend, and your schedule doesn't have a weekend in it.

authoring.premise: Your family wants to visit for a weekend, and your schedule doesn't have a weekend in it.

choices.label: Make it work
choices.result: You give them the guest room, practice in the morning and spend every evening with them. You're exhausted and happy.

choices.label: Ask them to come in the offseason
choices.result: You ask them to wait for the offseason. {parent} understands; {sibling} is disappointed.

choices.label: Bring them to practice
choices.result: You get them passes to a practice and lunch with the team. {sibling} talks about it for months.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Attention
scenarios.text: Someone recognizes you at the grocery store and follows you down three aisles, talking the whole time.

authoring.premise: Someone recognizes you at the grocery store and won't stop talking.

choices.label: Be gracious
choices.result: You stop, talk and take a photo. It costs you ten minutes and makes someone's week.

choices.label: Keep moving, politely
choices.result: You smile, say thanks and keep moving. They post that you were 'a little cold'.

choices.label: Shop at night
choices.result: You start shopping at eleven at night. Nobody recognizes you, and the cereal aisle is all yours.

scenarios.title: The Local Radio Appearance
scenarios.text: A sports radio show invites you on, live, during drive time.

authoring.premise: A sports radio show invites you on, live, during drive time.

choices.label: Prepare and go
choices.result: You prepare three stories and keep it light. The host invites you back.

choices.label: Wing it
choices.result: You go on without notes. One joke lands; one answer about the coaching staff gets replayed all week.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline politely and spend the hour at the net.

scenarios.title: The Practice Routine
scenarios.text: Your college routine isn't working at this level, and you need a new one by Sunday.

authoring.premise: Your college routine isn't working at this level, and you need a new one by Sunday.

choices.label: Copy the veteran's routine
choices.result: You copy the veteran snapper's pre-kick routine step for step. It feels strange, then it feels like yours.

choices.label: Build your own
choices.result: You build your own routine from scratch, charting every kick for a week.

choices.label: Ask {coach}
choices.result: You ask {coach} to help you build it. The coach is pleased you asked.

authoring.premise: A sales rep wants you on expensive new training equipment, with a price to match.

scenarios.title: The First Contract Question
scenarios.text: A reporter asks whether you expect an extension, and you haven't kicked a regular-season game yet.

authoring.premise: A reporter asks whether you expect an extension, and you haven't kicked a regular-season game.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and say you're just trying to keep your locker. The quote is charming, and nobody reads into it.

choices.label: Say you've earned a look
choices.result: You say you think you've earned a look. The front office reads it, and so does the veteran kicker.

choices.label: Decline to answer
choices.result: You say contracts are your agent's job. It's dull and smart.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Struggle
scenarios.text: A fellow rookie is falling apart: late to meetings, quiet at lunch, gone the minute practice ends.

authoring.premise: A fellow rookie is falling apart, and nobody else seems to notice.

choices.label: Check on him
choices.result: You knock on his door after practice and stay for an hour. He doesn't say much, but he shows up early the next day.

choices.label: Tell a veteran
choices.result: You quietly tell a veteran you trust. The veteran handles it better than you could have.

choices.label: Mind your own business
choices.result: You've got your own roster spot to worry about. He's released a month later, and you think about it longer than you expected.

scenarios.title: The Family Expectations
scenarios.text: Your family expects more now that you're earning, and they're not shy about it.

authoring.premise: Your family expects more now that you're earning, and they're not shy about it.

choices.label: Set a family budget
choices.result: You sit down with {parent} and set a yearly amount for family help. It's awkward and it ends the guessing.

choices.label: Say yes to everything
choices.result: You say yes to every request. It feels good, and your account feels it more.

choices.label: Say not yet
choices.result: You explain that a rookie contract isn't forever money. Some of them understand.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Bill
scenarios.text: Your car's transmission dies the week before a road trip, and the repair costs more than the car is worth.

authoring.premise: A costly bill arrives at the worst possible time.

choices.label: Fix it
choices.result: You pay for the repair and take the bus to practice for a week. The veterans think it's hilarious.

choices.label: Buy something new
choices.result: You buy a new car the same day. It's lovely, and the payment is going to follow you around for years.

choices.label: Ask a teammate for rides
choices.result: You ask a teammate for rides until you figure it out. You become friends on those drives.

scenarios.title: The Former Coach Calls
scenarios.text: Your old college coach calls to check in, and asks how you're really doing.

authoring.premise: Your old college coach calls to check in, and asks how you're really doing.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.result: You tell the truth: it's harder than you expected. The coach tells you about every player who said the same thing and made it.

choices.label: Say everything's great
choices.result: You say everything's great. The coach doesn't believe you and says so, kindly.

choices.label: Ask for help
choices.result: You ask for help with one specific problem. The coach watches your film and calls back the next day.

scenarios.title: The Community Invitation
scenarios.text: A local school asks you to speak to its athletes about what it takes.

authoring.premise: A local school asks you to speak to its athletes.

choices.label: Speak honestly
choices.result: You tell them about the cuts, the doubts and the practice you nearly quit. Three kids stay after to ask questions.

choices.label: Run a kicking clinic instead
choices.result: You skip the speech and run a kicking clinic on their field. Everyone gets muddy.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: You decline because of the schedule. They invite someone else.

scenarios.title: The Dating Question
scenarios.text: Someone you meet at a teammate's dinner seems more interested in the league than in you.

authoring.premise: Someone you meet seems more interested in the league than in you.

choices.label: Ask them out anyway
choices.result: You ask them out. They ask a lot about the league, and a little about you. You don't call again, and you learn to spot it faster.

choices.label: Change the subject
choices.result: You keep steering the conversation away from football. By dessert, they're laughing at your terrible cooking stories.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: You thank the host and leave early. You'd rather be bored than be a résumé.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Celebration
scenarios.text: The locker room has a social scene: card games, a weekly dinner, a group that goes out after home games. You have to decide how far into it you want to go.

authoring.premise: The locker room has a social scene, and you have to decide how far into it you want to go.

choices.label: Go all in, within reason
choices.result: You join the card game and the weekly dinner, and skip the late nights. By midseason, you're part of the room.

choices.label: Pick one thing
choices.result: You pick the weekly dinner and nothing else. You know a few teammates well instead of all of them a little.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: You keep to yourself and your routine. Your kicking is sharp, and nobody invites you anywhere by October.

scenarios.title: The Position Meeting
scenarios.text: Your place on the depth chart comes up in a meeting you weren't invited to, and the long snapper tells you about it at lunch.

authoring.premise: Your place on the depth chart comes up in a meeting you weren't invited to.

choices.label: Ask {coach} directly
choices.result: You ask {coach} where you stand. It's an honest answer: safe, for now, if the next month looks like the last one.

choices.label: Kick and say nothing
choices.result: You say nothing and kick the best week of practice you've had.

choices.label: Call your agent
choices.result: You call your agent, who calls the general manager, who calls {coach}. Everyone knows you asked.

scenarios.title: The New Playbook
scenarios.text: A new coaching staff installs a new playbook and new expectations for the specialists, and the first test is Friday.

authoring.premise: A new coaching staff installs a new playbook and new expectations for the specialists.

choices.label: Learn it cold
choices.result: You learn the new special teams playbook cold, including the parts that aren't yours.

choices.label: Learn your part
choices.result: You learn your part perfectly and nothing else. It's enough.

choices.label: Study with the unit
choices.result: You set up a study session with the snapper and the holder. It turns into a unit dinner.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Comparison
scenarios.text: The media compare you with another young kicker, every week, by name.

authoring.premise: The media compare you with another young kicker, every week, by name.

choices.label: Call the other kicker
choices.result: You call the other kicker and laugh about it. You agree not to read anything with both your names in it.

choices.label: Use it
choices.result: You put the comparison on your locker and kick every practice like it's a contest.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You stop reading the coverage. It's quieter, and it takes discipline.

scenarios.title: The Charity Donation
scenarios.text: Your aunt asks you to donate to a cause back home: a new roof for the church you grew up in.

authoring.premise: A family member asks you to donate to a cause back home.

choices.label: Give generously
choices.result: You give more than she asked. The church puts your name on a plaque you'll be embarrassed by forever.

choices.label: Give what you planned
choices.result: You give the amount in your budget and explain why. She's a little disappointed and grateful anyway.

choices.label: Run a fundraiser instead
choices.result: You host a fundraiser in your hometown and raise twice the money, with your time instead of your account.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Advice
scenarios.text: A veteran explains, very calmly, how fast a career can end: his roommate from his rookie year lasted one season.

authoring.premise: A veteran explains, very calmly, how fast a career can end.

choices.label: Ask what he did differently
choices.result: You ask what he did differently. His answer has nothing to do with kicking: he saved, he slept, he showed up.

choices.label: Let it scare you
choices.result: It scares you, and you start saving half of every check and sleeping nine hours a night.

choices.label: Shrug it off
choices.result: You shrug and say it won't happen to you. The veteran nods slowly, like he's heard it before.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Warning
scenarios.text: Your agent warns you to be careful about where you're seen: a teammate's photo outside a club just cost him a sponsor.
